Long-term follow-up of the prospective Royal College of Gen- eral Practitioners’ study has found no overall increased risk of cancer.2 It is also worthy of note that two large prospective cohort studies (the Nurses’ Health Study and the Royal College of Gen- eral Practitioners’ study) found no evidence of a difference in overall mortality between women who had used oral contracep- tives and those who had not.3,4 Some general reviews on hormo- nal contraceptives and cancer are cited below.5-9 1.
